## Core web

### Causes (32)

- **Isolation & confinement → Psychological stress**: chronic high cortisol · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [mars500] [klos25]  
  Mars-500 (520 days, no microgravity or radiation) produced long-lasting high cortisol from isolation and confinement alone.
- **Isolation & confinement → Immune dysregulation**: fewer microbes → "immune amnesia" · 🧑⭐⭐ · [klos25] [ponomarev21] [mars500]  
  Mars-500 immune system was dysregulated rather than simply weak. A review of 140 ICE studies found dysregulation in every setting, mostly reversing afterwards. Antarctic crews had lower salivary immunoglobulins.
- **Psychological stress → Cortisol / HPA axis**: activates HPA axis · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [mehta17] [salivary]  
  Raises cortisol and DHEA. Long-duration flight also changed the daily salivary cortisol rhythm.
- **Psychological stress → Inflammation / oxidative stress**: adds inflammatory load · 🧑⭐ · [arterial20]  
  Psychological stress is one of several sources of oxidative and inflammatory damage (with radiation, low activity, poor nutrition and high oxygen during EVA).
- **Cortisol / HPA axis → Immune dysregulation**: weakens cellular immunity · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [mehta17] [salivary] [evrep] [crucian18]  
  On the ISS, crew who shed a latent virus had higher salivary cortisol. Reactivation was distinct to crew who did spacewalks (EVA).
- **Cortisol / HPA axis → Muscle loss**: muscle protein loss · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [inact]  
  After 14 days of bed rest, high cortisol tripled amino-acid loss from muscle.
- **Cortisol / HPA axis → Bone loss**: osteoclast activity ↑ · 🧑⭐ · ⚠️ no source yet  
  Clinical evidence: glucocorticoid therapy is a known cause of excess osteoclast activity, and cortisol is a glucocorticoid.
- **Cortisol / HPA axis → Insulin resistance (glucose)**: insulin resistance · 🧑⭐⭐ · [bedrest28]  
  Bed rest plus high cortisol: leg insulin sensitivity 9.1 → 5.2 mg/kg/min.
- **Space radiation → Inflammation / oxidative stress**: reactive oxygen species · 🐭🧫⭐⭐ · [willey] [zhang17] [wadhwa24]  
  Radiation and unloading share a mechanism: both raise oxidative stress.
- **Space radiation → Immune dysregulation**: lymphocytes most radio-sensitive · 🐭🧫🧑⭐⭐ · [proton] [hls_spe] [wadhwa24] [radiso] [wadhwa2024]  
  Dose-dependent lymphocyte drop after proton radiation (animals). Human lymphocytes show more chromosomal aberrations after long missions. A strong solar particle event plus simulated microgravity impaired bacterial clearance in mice.
- **Space radiation → Bone loss**: resorption ↑ then formation ↓ · 🐭⭐⭐ · [willey] [zhang17] [wadhwa2024]  
  Mouse tibia osteoclasts: radiation +46%, hindlimb unloading +47%, both combined +64%.
- **Space radiation → Blood vessels**: endothelial damage (deep space) · 🐭🧑⭐ · [delp16]  
  Apollo lunar astronauts: 43% cardiovascular deaths vs 9–11% for others, but only 3 of 7 people. In mice, deep-space-type radiation caused lasting damage to the vessel lining.
- **Microgravity → Immune dysregulation**: directly disrupts T-cell activation · 🧫🐭⭐⭐ · [chang]  
  Independent of stress hormones: a second route to weak T cells and viral reactivation.
- **Microgravity → Fluid shift**: blood moves headward · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [cvmeta] [norsk15]
- **Microgravity → Unloading / inactivity**: no weight-bearing · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [receptors]
- **Microgravity → Inflammation / oxidative stress**: oxidative stress · 🐭🧫⭐⭐ · [wadhwa24] [zhang17]  
  Inflammation from microgravity plus radiation can trigger bone loss.
- **Unloading / inactivity → Muscle loss**: atrophy · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [receptors] [muscgen]  
  Strongest link in the map. Happens despite exercise programmes.
- **Unloading / inactivity → Bone loss**: resorption ↑, formation ↓ · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [receptors] [osteoclast] [zhang17]  
  Microgravity impairs osteocytes and osteoblasts, so osteoclasts dominate.
- **Unloading / inactivity → Heart & blood pressure**: cardiac atrophy · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [perhonen01] [jacc23]  
  Left-ventricle mass fell ~12% after a short flight. Scott Kelly’s heart shrank ~0.74 g/week but still worked well.
- **Unloading / inactivity → Insulin resistance (glucose)**: inactivity → insulin resistance · 🧑⭐⭐ · [bedrest28] [vascular]
- **Fluid shift → Heart & blood pressure**: HR ↑ · BP ↓ · HRV ↓ · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [cvmeta] [norsk15] [autonomic] [crucian2018]  
  BP about 10 mmHg lower on long missions. After landing: orthostatic intolerance (fainting on standing).
- **Inflammation / oxidative stress → Immune dysregulation**: plasma cytokines ↑ · 🧑⭐⭐ · [crucian18] [wadhwa24]
- **Inflammation / oxidative stress → Bone loss**: RANKL → osteoclasts · 🐭🧫⭐⭐ · [receptors] [osteoclast] [wadhwa24]  
  RANKL binding RANK is required to make osteoclasts.
- **Inflammation / oxidative stress → Blood vessels**: oxidative damage · 🧑⭐ · [arterial20] [arteries25]  
  In LEO, biomarkers rose in flight but returned to baseline within a week, and arteries showed no thickening or stiffening over 5 years. Real deep-space risk; mostly theoretical for ISS-length missions.
- **Immune dysregulation → Bone loss**: T/B cells make RANKL (two-way) · 🐭🧫⭐⭐ · [receptors] [osteoclast]  
  Osteoimmunology: bone and immune cells share RANKL, so effects run both ways.
- **Muscle loss → Immune dysregulation**: myokines (IL-6) · 🐭⭐ · [il6] [muscgen]  
  Partly hypothesis. Post-exercise IL-6 scales with body weight; less IL-6 in space may explain why exercise does not fully stop loss.
- **Immune dysregulation → Latent virus reactivation**: T/NK ↓ → herpes reactivation · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [mehta17] [crucian18] [immrisk] [evrep] [thymus24]  
  Frequency and viral load rise with mission length. Resembles shingles patients, but milder. HSV-1 and VZV hide in cranial nerve ganglia, so reactivation is also a nervous-system event.
- **Latent virus reactivation → Illness & symptoms**: rash, cold sores, shingles · 🧑⭐⭐ · [crucian16] [hsv1] [shingles]  
  Most reactivation is asymptomatic. Cases include an HSV-1 rash lasting ~200 days and shingles with normal vital signs.
- **Insulin resistance (glucose) → Blood vessels**: stiffer arteries · 🧑⭐⭐ · [vascular]  
  CSA Vascular: carotid stiffness and insulin resistance rose together.
- **Psychological stress → Immune dysregulation**: HRV ↓ → stress ↑ → cortisol ↑ → latent virus reactivation · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [mehta2017] [crucian2018]  
  Chronic and acute psychological stress activates the HPA axis and suppresses cellular immunity, driving latent herpesvirus reactivation.
- **Sleep (actigraphy) → Immune dysregulation**: Sleep ↓ → cortisol ↑ → T cells ↓ → virus reactivation · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [barger2014] [mehta2017]  
  ISS astronauts average ~6 h of sleep; cumulative sleep deficiency raises cortisol and impairs T-cell immune surveillance.
- **EVA (spacewalk) → Immune dysregulation**: EVA → stress hormones ↑ → reactivation in EVA crew · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [iss_saliva2020] [mehta2017]  
  Extravehicular activity increases stress hormones and salivary viral shedding over the following 48–72 hours.

### Amplifies (2)

- **Microgravity → Psychological stress**: amplifies stress effects · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [inact]  
  Stress and microgravity multiply rather than add: inactivity makes muscle ~3× more responsive to cortisol.
- **Cortisol / HPA axis → Muscle loss**: Stress × inactivity → muscle loss amplified · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [ferrando2004]  
  Inactivity amplifies skeletal muscle catabolic response to hypercortisolemia multiplicatively rather than additively.

### Protects (4)

- **Exercise & loading → Heart & blood pressure**: offsets cardiac atrophy · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [jacc23] [jacc2023]  
  13-astronaut ISS study.
- **Exercise & loading → Muscle loss**: slows loss (partial) · 🧑⭐⭐ · [il6]  
  Loss continues despite exercise programmes.
- **Exercise & loading → Bone loss**: slows loss (partial) · 🧑⭐⭐ · [il6]
- **Exercise & loading → Muscle loss**: Low resistance exercise → unloading → muscle & bone loss · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [ferrando2004]  
  Daily ARED resistive exercise provides the mechanical loading needed to limit microgravity muscle atrophy and bone mineral loss.

### Confounds (7)

- **Fluid shift → Illness & symptoms**: puffy face & headache look like illness · 🧑 · [cvmeta]

- **Fluid shift → Resting HR vs own baseline**: raises HR → set baseline in flight · 🧑 · [cvmeta]  
  Other HR confounders: stress, intense exercise, medications, vaccination.
- **Fluid shift → HRV (ECG / PPG)**: lowers HRV baseline · 🧑 · [autonomic]
- **Fluid shift → Blood pressure**: lowers BP ~10 mmHg · 🧑 · [norsk15]
- **Fluid shift → Facial behaviour change**: puffy face changes geometry · ⚠️ no source yet  
  Set the facial baseline in flight. Astronauts are also trained to stay composed.
- **Fluid shift → Camera rPPG (RGB + NIR)**: may shift rPPG baseline (untested) · ⚠️ no source yet
- **Muscle loss → Inflammation / oxidative stress**: landing cytokine spike may be regeneration · 🧑 · [twinsland]  
  Twins Study re-analysis: inflammatory markers spiking at landing may reflect muscle repair, not illness. High cytokines are not always "sick".

## Nervous system extension

### Causes (11)

- **Psychological stress → Sympathetic / autonomic nervous system**: amygdala → hypothalamus → sympathetic activation · 🧑⭐⭐ · [capri25]  
  The same brain stress system drives the HPA axis (cortisol hub).
- **Sympathetic / autonomic nervous system → Immune dysregulation**: adrenergic immune modulation · 🧑⭐⭐ · [stowe03] [capri25]  
  Short flights (9 d): sympathetic responses dominate. Longer flights (16 d): cortisol-mediated changes at landing.
- **Sympathetic / autonomic nervous system → Heart & blood pressure**: HR ↑, HRV ↓ · 🧑⭐⭐ · [capri25] [autonomic]
- **Fluid shift → Brain structure & CSF**: brain shifts up, ventricles enlarge · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [mcgregor23] [vanombergen19] [hupfeld22]  
  Likely reduced CSF resorption in microgravity.
- **Fluid shift → Eyes (SANS)**: venous congestion, altered CSF flow · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [sans_wjg] [sansreview26] [sans_nasa23] [sans_sr20]  
  Not simply raised intracranial pressure.
- **Brain structure & CSF → Eyes (SANS)**: eye–brain axis (perivascular spaces) · 🧑⭐⭐ · [eyebrain23] [pvs]  
  Astronauts who developed SANS had larger white-matter perivascular spaces before and after flight.
- **Microgravity → Balance & motion sickness (vestibular)**: sensory mismatch · 🧑⭐⭐⭐ · [vestib15] [neurovest17] [reentry25]
- **Microgravity → Cognition & performance**: early-flight slowing (mild, reversible) · 🧑⭐⭐ · [cog24]  
  Head-down bed rest (fluid shift analog) also gives mild early slowing.
- **Space radiation → Cognition & performance**: deep-space CNS risk (rodents) · 🐭⭐ · [gcr18] [gcr23] [cucinotta]  
  Rodent deficits at ≥0.1 Gy heavy ions, but missions give <0.04 Gy/yr; some studies even show pro-cognitive effects. Uncertain.
- **Isolation & confinement → Inflammation / oxidative stress**: neuroinflammation (with microgravity) · 🐭⭐ · [mcat]  
  Mitochondrial ROS drove the brain immune response in mice.
- **Sleep (actigraphy) → Cognition & performance**: sleep loss → worse attention · 🧑⭐⭐ · [cog24]  
  Analog studies with sleep restriction; in ISS data no clear link was found.

### Confounds (1)

- **Balance & motion sickness (vestibular) → Illness & symptoms**: motion sickness looks like illness · 🧑 · [reentry25]  
  Malaise, appetite loss, headache.

- 🟢 **HRV (ECG / PPG) → Sympathetic / autonomic nervous system**: autonomic balance · [autonomic] [mentalhrv]

## Concepts

| id | Concept | Category | Layer | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `isolation` | Isolation & confinement | stressor | core | Always on, and grows with mission length. Acts mostly upstream through stress, plus a direct immune effect from meeting fewer new microbes. |
| `stress` | Psychological stress | stressor | core | The most useful factor to monitor: it varies day to day and reaches immune, muscle, bone, vessels and glucose through cortisol. Trackable with HRV, sleep and saliva cortisol. |
| `radiation` | Space radiation | stressor | core | Varies with solar events and is already tracked by dosimeters. Hits lymphocytes, bone and, in deep space, blood vessels. |
| `microgravity` | Microgravity | stressor | core | The biggest cause in the map (muscle, bone, heart, direct immune effect, and it amplifies stress). Because it never changes, track its variable version: exercise and loading logs. |
| `cortisol` | Cortisol / HPA axis | hub | core | Stress hormone hub (with DHEA). Connects stress to immune suppression, muscle breakdown, bone resorption and insulin resistance. |
| `inflam` | Inflammation / oxidative stress | hub | core | The main hub. Shared signalling molecules (IL-6, RANKL, TNF-α) link the immune system, bone, muscle and blood vessels. Radiation and unloading both raise oxidative stress. |
| `fluidshift` | Fluid shift | hub | core | Blood moves toward the head: puffy face, headache, stuffy head, flu-like feeling. Changes HR, HRV and BP baselines and can look like illness, so it confounds several signals. |
| `unloading` | Unloading / inactivity | hub | core | No weight-bearing, so muscle, bone and heart shrink together. Inactivity also makes muscle about 3× more sensitive to cortisol. |
| `exercise` | Exercise & loading | counter | core | The one countermeasure that protects muscle, bone and heart together. Fully offsets cardiac atrophy; only slows muscle and bone loss. |
| `immune` | Immune dysregulation | body | core | About 50% of astronauts. White-cell counts look normal, but T-cell and NK-cell function drops and plasma cytokines rise. Lasts the whole 6-month mission. NASA: still unclear whether it causes more disease. |
| `glucose` | Insulin resistance (glucose) | body | core | Fasting insulin was elevated in flight in all astronauts (CSA Vascular). Bed rest plus high cortisol: leg insulin sensitivity 9.1 → 5.2 mg/kg/min. CGMs already used in space research. |
| `bone` | Bone loss | body | core | Osteoclasts dominate: resorption up, formation down. Hit from four directions: unloading, radiation, cortisol and inflammation (RANKL). |
| `muscle` | Muscle loss | body | core | Atrophy continues despite exercise programmes. Muscle also signals back to immunity through myokines such as IL-6. |
| `heart` | Heart & blood pressure | body | core | HR up, BP down ~10 mmHg, HRV down. Left-ventricle mass −12% after a short flight. A smaller heart can still be healthy (normal adaptation vs a problem). Fainting on standing after landing. |
| `vessels` | Blood vessels | body | core | Real risk for deep space (Apollo data, mouse radiation studies), but in low Earth orbit arteries showed no thickening or stiffening over 5 years. |
| `viral` | Latent virus reactivation | outcome | core | EBV, VZV, CMV and HSV-1 shed by 53% of shuttle and 61% of ISS astronauts. Rises with mission length. Mostly without symptoms. |
| `symptoms` | Illness & symptoms | outcome | core | ISS records: skin rashes 1.12 per flight-year, upper respiratory 0.97. 46% of crew had a notable event. In one shingles case vital signs stayed normal, so symptom logging matters. |
| `wearables` | Wearables (Astroskin, ARCHeR) | device | core | Already flown: Astroskin smart shirt on ISS since 2018 (ECG, BP, SpO₂, breathing, skin temp, activity), Garmin on Polaris Dawn, ARCHeR wristbands on Artemis II. Hardware is mostly solved; the software that fuses signals is the gap. |
| `rppg` | Camera rPPG (RGB + NIR) | device | core | Contact-free HR, HRV and breathing from facial colour changes. RGB+NIR fusion is most robust. Not yet validated on astronauts in orbit: an opportunity. Hackathon-friendly with a webcam and rPPG-Toolbox. |
| `missionday` | Mission day count | signal 🟢 | core | Free proxy for isolation load and for viral reactivation risk, which grows with mission length. |
| `saliva` | Saliva cortisol + viral DNA | signal 🟢 | core | Reads the stress → virus chain directly. Needs a lab, but saliva is easy to collect; used on ISS and Artemis II. |
| `sweat` | Sweat cortisol | signal 🔵 | core | Direct hormone reading, but only prototypes; some need visible sweat; not tested in space. |
| `cgm` | CGM (glucose) | signal 🟢 | core | Continuous glucose monitors are already used in space health research. |
| `symptomlog` | Symptom log | signal 🟢 | core | Rash, sore throat, fatigue. Open question: how to collect it without annoying a busy crew. |
| `face` | Facial behaviour change | signal 🟡 | core | Faces are not reliable emotion readers; drop micro-expressions. Useful only as one input in fusion, as change from the person’s own baseline. Frame as medical/safety under the EU AI Act; crew own their data. |
| `bp` | Blood pressure | signal 🔴 | core | Stress raises it ~7 mmHg, but spaceflight lowers it ~10 mmHg. Weak stress signal. |
| `hrv` | HRV (ECG / PPG) | signal 🟢 | core | Stress shifts it toward sympathetic, and that response is unchanged in space. Baseline is lowered by microgravity, so compare to the astronaut’s own in-flight baseline. |
| `restHR` | Resting HR vs own baseline | signal 🟢 | core | Smartwatch study: 63% of COVID cases flaggable before symptoms; LSTM autoencoder (LAAD) flagged 92%. Catches symptomatic infection, not silent viral shedding. |
| `sleep` | Sleep (actigraphy) | signal 🟢 | core | Astronauts average ~6 h vs 8.5 h scheduled; ~75% used sleep meds. Both a cause and a symptom of stress. |
| `scans` | Scans & strength tests | signal 🔴 | core | Only way to see muscle and bone change, and it is slow. No daily reading. |
| `exerciselog` | Exercise / loading log | signal 🟢 | core | The variable version of microgravity: how much loading each astronaut actually got. |
| `dosimeter` | Radiation dosimeter | signal 🟢 | core | Already exists on every mission; captures dose spikes from solar events. |
| `sns` | Sympathetic / autonomic nervous system | hub | nervous | The stress system lives in the brain: amygdala → hypothalamus → both the HPA axis (cortisol) and the sympathetic nervous system. Sympathetic responses dominate after short flights; cortisol-driven changes dominate after longer ones. HRV is a direct read-out of this system. |
| `brain` | Brain structure & CSF | body | nervous | Brain shifts upward in the skull; ventricles enlarge ~11–25%. Growth slows after ~6 months and recovers only partly 6–12 months after landing. Crews with <3 years between missions showed little further enlargement. Medical meaning still unclear. |
| `sans` | Eyes (SANS) | body | nervous | Spaceflight-associated neuro-ocular syndrome: optic disc edema, globe flattening, choroidal folds, hyperopic shift. ~81% of NASA long-duration astronauts had at least one finding; ~66% show the earliest sign. So far vision effects have been correctable with glasses. |
| `vestibular` | Balance & motion sickness (vestibular) | body | nervous | Sensory mismatch in microgravity: ~70% of astronauts have space motion sickness or impaired motor performance, mostly resolving within 1 h to 4 days. Re-entry motion sickness is worse after long missions and does not reliably improve with repeat flights. |
| `cognition` | Cognition & performance | outcome | nervous | 25 ISS astronauts: no systematic decline on 6-month missions. Early flight: slower processing speed, visual working memory, sustained attention. Late flight: slower emotion recognition. Processing speed recovered only after return. |
| `cogtest` | Cognition test battery | signal 🟢 | nervous | Computerised tests (Cognition battery, WinSCAT). WinSCAT is a medical requirement for US long-duration crew. |
| `oct` | Eye imaging (OCT) | signal 🔵 | nervous | Optical coherence tomography detects optic disc edema and globe changes; in-flight imaging and AI detection are improving. |
| `mri` | Brain MRI | signal 🔴 | nervous | Only pre- and post-flight; not available in orbit. |
| `eva` | EVA (spacewalk) | stressor | core | Extravehicular activity causes acute physical load, sleep disruption, and elevated stress hormones linked to latent viral reactivation. |
